info.title: Bulwark API
info.description: Unified security scanning: submit a scan, watch progress, read findings.

get.description: Projects (plan §27): one row per distinct repository, most recently scanned first.

Plan §28.1's project overview: verdict, fix-first queue, since-previous-scan deltas,
the open-issue trend, and what the latest scan did (and didn't) cover. See
core/persistence/repo.py's asset-overview functions and docs/v2-week33-verification.md for
exactly how each field is derived from existing scan/issue data.

post.description:
Register a web/DAST target (plan §22.4). Returns the proof-of-control instructions for
the chosen method; no campaign (Week 49 task 3) can run against this asset until `POST
/assets/{id}/verify` passes against a live DNS/HTTP check, not merely this call.

Runs a real, live DNS/HTTP check right now and persists the result -- never trusts a
previously-stored "verified" status, since ownership can lapse any time after it passed.

Start a DAST campaign (plan §22.4): gated on a LIVE ownership check right now (never a
cached "verified" status) and, for an active campaign, the rate limit -- both checked before
a Scan row is even created, so an unverified or rate-limited attempt never shows up as a
queued campaign waiting to run and fail.

schema.title: Response List Dast Campaigns Assets  Asset Id  Campaigns Get

get.description:
Plan §28.3's issues table: the asset's currently-open issues (its latest scan's
findings, joined with each one's triage state). Empty, not 404, when nothing has scanned
yet -- mirrors `/scans/{id}/findings`'s own shape so the same frontend table component
can render either.

parameters.name: triage

schema.description: Filter TO these triage statuses (e.g. accepted, not_a_risk). Omitted: the active queue -- untouched issues, plus any accepted issue past its expiry.
schema.title: Triage

parameters.description: Filter TO these triage statuses (e.g. accepted, not_a_risk). Omitted: the active queue -- untouched issues, plus any accepted issue past its expiry.

parameters.name: sla

schema.description: Filter to these SLA states: on_track, due_soon, breached (plan §44.1). Nothing matches when the project has no SLA policy.
schema.title: Sla

parameters.description: Filter to these SLA states: on_track, due_soon, breached (plan §44.1). Nothing matches when the project has no SLA policy.

parameters.name: priority

schema.description: Filter to these priority bands: P1, P2, P3, P4 (plan §44.3).
schema.title: Priority

parameters.description: Filter to these priority bands: P1, P2, P3, P4 (plan §44.3).

get.description:
Plan §20.5's Dependencies screen: the asset's latest scan's SBOM (`syft` in its
`tools`), if any. Empty, not 404, when no scan has opted into it yet -- same shape as
`/assets/{id}/issues`.

The one issue's own detail screen (plan §28.3): the same Finding shape as a row in the
issues table, fetched on its own rather than paging through the whole list.

schema.title: Response Get One Issue Assets  Asset Id  Issues  Issue Id  Get

post.description:
Mark not-a-risk (needs a reason) or accept risk (needs an expiry), or reopen either
decision -- plan §28.3: "Both write to the audit log." `asset_id` in the path is a
readability/routing convenience (matches the frontend's URLs); the org check that actually
matters is `_get_asset` below, before the issue lookup even runs.

Same rule per issue as the single-issue endpoint, applied to a batch: one issue failing
(not found in this org, or a bad request for that action) doesn't abort the rest -- each
success still gets its own audit entry, exactly as if triaged one at a time.

schema.title: Response Get Issue History Assets  Asset Id  Issues  Issue Id  History Get

get.description: Reference guidance (CWE + OWASP) and any cached AI suggestion. Calls no model.

post.description: Generate (or fetch cached) an AI suggestion. Sends data to the model provider.

Start the verified-fix agent for one issue (plan §21.2): propose a patch, verify it
(rerun the rule, rerun scanners, optionally the project's own tests), then wait for a human
to approve or reject before a pull request is ever opened. Runs as a Temporal workflow --
`409` if Temporal is unreachable, `429` over this organization's concurrency cap
(ADR-0015).

A human approving the proposed patch (plan §21.2: never auto-merge). Only meaningful
while the run is `awaiting_approval`; signalling any other state is harmless (Temporal
just records a signal an already-finished workflow never reads).

schema.title: Response Approve Verified Fix Assets  Asset Id  Issues  Issue Id  Verified Fix Approve Post
Response Reject Verified Fix Assets  Asset Id  Issues  Issue Id  Verified Fix Reject Post

post.description:
Ask the triage assistant for a verdict on one issue (plan §21.3): reads the taint path
and surrounding code from its latest occurrence and returns an advisory verdict. Stored so
`core.risk.score` can use it as one ranking input on this asset's later scans -- never
changes `triage_status` or anything else about the issue; a person still decides that.

Generate Hypotheses-lane candidates for one asset (plan §21.4): re-checks out its latest
scan's source, finds every route with no recognized auth marker in a file where a sibling
route has one (`core.hypotheses.facts`, deterministic, no model), and asks the model to
decide which of those are worth a person's time. Off by default: `409` when no model is
routed for `Task.HYPOTHESES` (the same on/off switch the gateway gives every task).

schema.title: Response List Hypotheses Endpoint Assets  Asset Id  Hypotheses Get

post.description:
A human confirming a hypothesis (plan §21.4): creates a real Issue, `source=
"llm-confirmed"`. Never automatic -- this is the one and only way that value is ever set.

schema.title: Response Dismiss Hypothesis Endpoint Assets  Asset Id  Hypotheses  Hypothesis Id  Dismiss Post

get.description:
The project's threat-model draft (plan §21.7). Auto-generated from the latest scan on
first access -- deterministic, no model call, so there is no cost gate to ask for first.
Once a person edits it or explicitly regenerates, that becomes the current row and stays
until the next explicit regenerate.

put.description:
A person's own edit to the diagram/table -- stored as-is, source="edited". Never
validated against the code: there is nothing to validate a person's own review notes
against.

post.description: Discards the current draft, including any edits, and regenerates from the latest scan.

get.description:
How long this organization keeps a scan's encrypted artifacts before crypto-shredding
them (plan §22.2). Always returns a value -- the plan's own default (7 days) when this org
has never set its own, never a 404.

Every plugin discovered via the `bulwark.scanner_adapters` entry point (Week 51 task 1,
plan §23), whether or not this organization has allowlisted it yet. `allowed` is this org's
allowlist row right now -- `core.plugins.signing` still re-verifies the image's Sigstore
signature at the moment a scan actually uses it, so `allowed=True` is not itself a guarantee
the plugin will run successfully.

schema.title: Response List Plugins Endpoint Plugins Get

put.description:
Trusting a plugin is security-relevant (it will run inside the same sandbox as a built-in
scanner) -- recorded in the audit log by `core.persistence.repo.set_plugin_allowed` itself.
Turning a plugin ON re-verifies its Sigstore signature synchronously, right now, so a bad
publisher identity or an unsigned image fails loudly at the moment someone tries to trust it
rather than silently at the next scan that happens to request it; turning one off never
needs that check.

get.description:
Week 51 task 2, plan §23. Never a 404 -- an org with nothing configured just shows every
integration as not configured, the same "always a value, never a missing-row error" posture
`GET /settings/retention` already has.

Every attack path chained from this asset's current open issues, ranked highest risk
first (plan §21.6, §28.5). Always computable without a model -- narrative generation
(Task.ATTACK_PATH) is best-effort per path (at most the first 10, by rank) and never blocks
the graph itself.

schema.title: Response List Attack Paths Endpoint Assets  Asset Id  Attack Paths Get

post.description:
Start a copilot conversation for one asset (plan §21.5). `409` if the copilot isn't
enabled, there's no completed scan, or the asset isn't git-sourced -- the same checks the
Hypotheses lane's own generate endpoint makes, since both need a real checkout.

Ask the copilot one question in an existing conversation (plan §21.5): clones the
asset's latest scan's source on the conversation's first message (cached for later
messages in the same conversation, core.copilot.session), then runs the tool-calling loop.
A model that never produces a validly-cited answer within its turn budget still gets a
stored, honest response -- never a 5xx for "the copilot couldn't find a grounded answer."

schema.title: Response List Copilot Messages Assets  Asset Id  Copilot Conversations  Conversation Id  Messages Get

get.description:
Plan §28.6: two scans of the same project, side by side -- new, fixed, reintroduced and
unchanged issues. 404s (not 400) when the two scans don't share an asset, the same
not-a-403 reasoning as `_get_scan` (ADR-0013): which other scans exist to compare against
isn't information a scan in a different org (or asset) should be able to probe for.

parameters.name: against

schema.description: The other scan id to compare against.
schema.title: Against

parameters.description: The other scan id to compare against.

get.description:
Plan §23's cost-per-scan dashboard (Week 50): an estimate, computed fresh on every call
rather than stored -- a scan's LLM spend keeps growing after the scan job itself finishes
(remediation suggestions, hypotheses, copilot messages are all requested later), so a cost
written once at completion would go stale the moment someone asks for a suggestion.

The same estimate as `get_scan_cost`, aggregated over every scan in the window -- an
internal visibility dashboard (plan §23), not a billing export.
Download the whole scan (every finding, ranked) as SARIF 2.1.0, HTML, PDF or JSON.

Response List Parsers V2 Parsers Get

Response Dedup Preview V2 Projects  Project Id  Dedup Preview Post

put.description:
Accepted, not finished: every Issue is re-ranked in the background, and the policy stays
locked until that is done. Poll the GET for progress.

schema.title: Response Project Acceptances V2 Projects  Project Id  Risk Acceptances Get
Response All Acceptances V2 Risk Acceptances Get

days.title: Days
days.description: Whole days from the request to the expiry.

can_decide.title: Can Decide
can_decide.description: Whether the caller may approve or reject it.

names.title: Names
names.description: Each actor's token name, to show people, not prefixes.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Every field a mapping can fill.

digest.title: Digest
digest.description: The `digest` of the preview being confirmed.

open_issue_count.title: Open Issue Count
open_issue_count.description: Open issues as of the latest completed scan; 0 if no scan has completed yet.

AssetSummary.title: AssetSummary
AssetSummary.description: A project (plan §27) — one distinct repository/archive, org-scoped (ADR-0012, ADR-0013).

sniffed_type.title: Sniffed Type
sniffed_type.description: What the bytes are, whatever they were called.

active_content.title: Active Content
active_content.description: HTML, SVG, XML or PDF: could run script if rendered.

AttackPathView.title: AttackPathView
AttackPathView.description:
One ranked attack path (plan §21.6, §28.5). `narrative` is `None` when no model is routed
for Task.ATTACK_PATH -- unlike the copilot, this never 409s for that: the graph itself (nodes,
edges, ranking, cheapest_link) is always real and useful without a model, only the prose
description is best-effort on top of it.

days.title: Days
days.description: Days from first detection to fix; null: no deadline.

warn.title: Warn
warn.description: 'Due soon' in the last this-many days.

file.title: File
file.description: A sample of the report, at most 2 MB.

use_model.title: Use Model
use_model.description: Ask the model for the draft when one is set up.

source.title: Source
source.description: The tool's name, if you know it.

test.title: Test
test.description: Test name; defaults to the parser's name.

test_id.title: Test Id
test_id.description: An existing Test; overrides the above.

parser.title: Parser
parser.description: Skip detection; see GET /v2/parsers, or `universal:<id>` for a saved mapping (GET /v2/mappings).

close_missing.title: Close Missing
close_missing.description: Close Issues this file no longer lists.

wait_for_dedup.title: Wait For Dedup
wait_for_dedup.description: Hold the response until the import is matched to Issues (its `dedup_complete`), up to 20 s; the 202 then carries its resting status. Otherwise poll GET /v2/imports/{id}.

preview.title: Preview
preview.description: Compute the counts, save nothing, keep the file.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Comma-separated; defaults to bandit, semgrep, gitleaks, trivy, osv-scanner.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Each item: {issue_id, error} — one issue failing (e.g. not found in this org) doesn't abort the rest of the batch.

records.title: Records
records.description: Where the records are; null for a CSV file.

status.title: Status
status.description: never_run, ok, empty, failing or disabled.

warning.title: Warning
warning.description: What the health screen should say, if anything.

vector.title: Vector
vector.description: Normalized: metrics in the specification's order.

rating.title: Rating
rating.description: FIRST's rating: None, Low, Medium, High, Critical.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Bulwark's severity; a 0.0 score is INFO.

name.title: Name
name.description: Empty for a valid CWE the bundled catalogue does not describe.

scan_id.title: Scan Id
scan_id.description: The scan this SBOM came from; null if there is none.

packages.title: Packages
packages.description: Each: name, version, ecosystem, purl, license, path, relation (direct|transitive|root|unknown), depends_on (purls), scorecard (or null).

DependenciesView.title: DependenciesView
DependenciesView.description:
Plan §20.5's Dependencies screen: one project's latest SBOM (`Scan.sbom_summary`), or an
empty view when no scan has opted into `syft` yet -- never a 404, matching
`/assets/{id}/issues`'s own "empty, not missing" shape.

FeedsStatus.title: FeedsStatus
FeedsStatus.description: State of the exploit-likelihood feeds behind risk scores. Empty until the first download.

generated.title: Generated
generated.description: How many NEW hypotheses this run surfaced and stored.

ai.description: A previously generated AI suggestion, if one is cached.

ai_enabled.title: Ai Enabled
ai_enabled.description: Whether this server can generate AI suggestions.

HypothesisView.title: HypothesisView
HypothesisView.description:
One Hypotheses-lane candidate (plan §21.4) -- off by default, its own tab, excluded from the
risk score and policy gates until a person promotes it. `promoted_issue_id` is set only once
`status` is "promoted".

detached.title: Detached
detached.description: Issues this file stopped listing that stay open because another source still reports them. Not 'closed': they are not fixed.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How sure format detection was; null when the caller named the parser.

duplicate.title: Duplicate
duplicate.description: True when this exact file was already the Test's latest import: nothing was queued, and `import_id` is the original's.

status.title: Status
status.description: queued, processing, previewed, applied, duplicate, failed, cancelled, reverted

dedup_complete.title: Dedup Complete
dedup_complete.description: True once the import has been matched to Issues by the project's deduplication settings (plan §42.3) -- which happens inside the import itself, so this is true from the moment the import leaves queued and processing (applied, previewed, duplicate, reverted, cancelled or failed: nothing is pending).

IntegrationSettingsView.title: IntegrationSettingsView
IntegrationSettingsView.description:
Never echoes a secret value back (Week 51 task 2, plan §23) -- a webhook URL, a GitHub PAT,
and a Jira API token are each themselves a bearer credential. `*_configured` says whether one is
set; the non-secret fields (which repo/project an issue gets filed into) are shown in full since
they're just config, not something that grants access on their own.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Only when there is no CVSS vector.

related_issue_id.title: Related Issue Id
related_issue_id.description: An automated Issue on the same handler with a related CWE, whose taint path this finding carries.

parser.title: Parser
parser.description: What to pass as `parser` to POST /v2/ingest.

recommended_dedup.title: Recommended Dedup
recommended_dedup.description: The deduplication strategy that suits this source (plan §42.2); every source is matched by `fingerprint_v2` until a project chooses (GET /v2/projects/{id}/dedup).

PluginView.title: PluginView
PluginView.description:
One discovered third-party scanner-adapter plugin (Week 51 task 1, plan §23). `allowed`
reflects the calling organization's own allowlist row right now -- it is not re-verified against
Sigstore here (that only happens when a scan actually requests this tool); a plugin can show
`allowed=True` and still fail at scan time if its image's signature has since gone bad.

can_approve.title: Can Approve
can_approve.description: False with the shared token: it could be anyone.

moved.title: Moved
moved.description: How many of the new top 50 change rank (or are new to it).

dropped.title: Dropped
dropped.description: In the top 50 now, not under these weights.

version.title: Version
version.description: 0 until someone saves a policy: priority is the v2 score.

weights.title: Weights
weights.description: In force; with no policy, v2's equivalents.

locked.title: Locked
locked.description: True while a recomputation runs; saving is refused.

verdict_count.title: Verdict Count
verdict_count.description: Critical/high-severity, currently-reachable issues from the latest scan's risk-ranked top items — the plan's calm-by-default rule (§29.2): an unreachable critical doesn't inflate this count.

fix_first.title: Fix First
fix_first.description: Same Finding shape as FindingsPage.items, risk-sorted, from the latest scan.

since_previous_scan.title: Since Previous Scan
since_previous_scan.description: fixed/new/returned since the scan before this one (ADR-0012's issue states); not a literal 7-day calendar window.

ProjectOverview.title: ProjectOverview
ProjectOverview.description:
Plan §28.1's project overview screen, built entirely from existing scan/issue data —
see core/persistence/repo.py's asset-overview functions for how each field is derived.

last_import.description: The Test's current snapshot: what the next upload is compared with.

spec.title: Spec
spec.description: A draft: review every field before saving.

status.title: Status
status.description: pending, running, done, failed, or superseded.

created.title: Created
created.description: False when the same finding was already recorded.

source_asset_id.title: Source Asset Id
source_asset_id.description: Optionally link to an existing git/archive project (plan §22.4, Week 49 task 4): its SAST scans' route map is what lets a later DAST finding be marked 'confirmed at runtime.' Must belong to the same organization.

RegisterWebAssetRequest.title: RegisterWebAssetRequest
RegisterWebAssetRequest.description:
Registering a DAST target (plan §22.4) -- this alone does not authorize scanning it; the
returned instructions must be satisfied and `/verify` must pass before a campaign can start.

source.title: Source
source.description: 'ai' (written by a model) or 'static' (reference text, no model).

label.title: Label
label.description: Always shown with the content, e.g. 'AI suggestion: review before applying'.

suggested_patch.title: Suggested Patch
suggested_patch.description: A unified diff as TEXT. Bulwark never applies it.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: Confidence in the fix, not in whether the finding is real.

tokens_used.title: Tokens Used
tokens_used.description: Tokens this call actually spent; 0 for static text or a cache hit.

RemediationView.title: RemediationView
RemediationView.description: Guidance for one finding. `source` says whether a model wrote it.

RetentionSettingsView.title: RetentionSettingsView
RetentionSettingsView.description:
How long this organization keeps a scan's encrypted artifacts before crypto-shredding them
(Week 47 task 2, plan §22.2). Never having set one returns the plan's own default (7 days), not
an error or a null -- there is always an effective policy, even if no row exists for it yet.

scan_id.title: Scan Id
scan_id.description: The scan the routes come from; null when none has any.

SaveIntegrationSettingsRequest.title: SaveIntegrationSettingsRequest
SaveIntegrationSettingsRequest.description:
A full replacement of this organization's integration settings (same semantics as
`SaveRetentionSettingsRequest`'s single value, just over more fields): a field omitted here is
cleared, not left unchanged. Re-fetch via `GET /settings/integrations` and resend every field
you want to keep.

ScanComparisonView.title: ScanComparisonView
ScanComparisonView.description: Plan §28.6's scan comparison screen: two of an asset's scans, side by side.

ScanCostView.title: ScanCostView
ScanCostView.description:
Plan §23's cost-per-scan dashboard (Week 50) -- an estimate, not a bill; see
core/observability/cost.py's own docstring for what it does and doesn't account for.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Defaults to the five default tools: bandit, semgrep, gitleaks, trivy, osv-scanner.

raw_findings.title: Raw Findings
raw_findings.description: Sum of every tool's findings before correlation.

dedup_rate.title: Dedup Rate
dedup_rate.description: 1 - unique/raw; 0 when there were no findings.

issue_counts.title: Issue Counts
issue_counts.description: Findings by Issue lifecycle state (new/open/reintroduced) for this scan's asset. Empty for scans that didn't finish 'completed', since only a full scan can tell an issue was fixed; see ADR-0012.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: severity, or priority (the P1-P4 band of each Issue).

version.title: Version
version.description: 0 until someone saves a policy; the starter values are shown.

counts.title: Counts
counts.description: Issues by SLA state, under the policy in force.

version.title: Version
version.description: 0 until someone chooses: the default applies.

recommended.title: Recommended
recommended.description: What suits this source, when we know it.

issues_seen.title: Issues Seen
issues_seen.description: Distinct Issues this source has reported (approximate).

StartConversationRequest.title: StartConversationRequest
StartConversationRequest.description:
Optional page context the panel was opened from (plan §28.6: "keeps page context"). Purely
informational -- never used for authorization, and never required to start a conversation.

StartDastCampaignRequest.title: StartDastCampaignRequest
StartDastCampaignRequest.description:
Start a DAST campaign (plan §22.4, Week 49 task 3) against an already ownership-verified web
Asset. "passive" (ZAP baseline only) runs unconditionally once verification passes; "active"
(adds curated Nuclei) is rate-limited to one per asset per
`core.dast.campaign.ACTIVE_SCAN_MIN_INTERVAL`.

ThreatModelView.title: ThreatModelView
ThreatModelView.description:
A project's threat-model draft (plan §21.7): a Mermaid data-flow diagram plus a STRIDE
table, generated from code intelligence -- a starting point for a person's own review, not an
assessment. `source` says whether the current content is the last generate output or a
person's own edit.

TriageAssistantView.title: TriageAssistantView
TriageAssistantView.description:
A model's verdict on one Issue (plan §21.3) -- advisory only, distinct from `IssueView`'s
`triage_status` (a human decision, ADR-0012). `null` if the assistant has never run for this
issue, which is the normal state until someone asks for one.

run_tests.title: Run Tests
run_tests.description: Also run the project's own test suite as part of verification. Only takes effect when the asset is linked to a verified GitHub App installation (plan §21.2); silently ignored otherwise, never a 4xx for asking.

test_image.title: Test Image
test_image.description: A Docker image to run tests in, e.g. 'python:3.12-slim'. Required when run_tests is true.

test_command.title: Test Command
test_command.description: Shell command to install deps and run tests, e.g. 'pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest -q'. Required when run_tests is true.

status.title: Status
status.description: running | awaiting_approval | approved | rejected | opened_pr | failed | inconclusive

latest_patch.title: Latest Patch
latest_patch.description: explanation/patch/confidence/tokens_used for the most recent attempt, once one has passed verification.

verification_record.title: Verification Record
verification_record.description: Every attempt's own verification steps, in order -- the audit trail ADR-0015 requires.

ended_reason.title: Ended Reason
ended_reason.description: Which limit ended a non-normal run: overall_timeout | per_attempt_timeout | max_attempts_exhausted | approval_timeout, or null for a normal approve/reject/opened_pr.
